Finding: Booking lead time is the primary no-show driver
Evidence: V=0.252 full data; V=0.237 holdout (T1 PASS)
Recommendation it supports: R1 targeted reminders, R2 confirmations, R3 scheduling policy

Finding: Previous no-show history is the secondary driver
Evidence: V=0.125 full data; V=0.101 holdout (T1 PASS)

Finding: Drivers compound: long lead + 2+ prior no-shows reaches 73% no-show
Evidence: Compounding matrix validated against raw data
Recommendation it supports: Prioritise the overlapping segment first (R1+R2 union)

Finding: The 4-rule risk tier separates risk and generalises
Evidence: High 71.94% full / 68.42% holdout; Low 30.9%/32.6%; all 5 splits PASS
Recommendation it supports: Operational triage at booking — no model required; benchmark for DS (T6)

Finding: Reminder coverage is flat across risk levels — the operational gap
Evidence: High tier 38.9% vs Low tier 87.3% covered; 660 long-lead unreached
Recommendation it supports: R1: redirect reminder capacity to long-lead, high-risk bookings

Finding: Reminder association is robust but associational
Evidence: Adjusted OR=0.830, p=0.006 (T3); unadjusted fails on holdout (T1)
Recommendation it supports: Rely on T4 randomised test for causal confirmation before scaling claims
